harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up a nightly backup pipeline: node1 pulls /srv/inventory/data from node2 over SSH each night via /usr/local/bin/backup-inventory.sh, storing dated tar.gz archives in /var/backups/inventory and pruning to the 7 most recent. Installed via /etc/cron.d/backup-inventory (0 2 * * *, runs as antrieb). Verified retention logic by simulating 8 days of archives and confirming the oldest was pruned. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on both node1 and node2: captured healthy baselines, rebooted each node one at a time, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified full recovery (cron active, SSH connectivity, backup script runs successfully end-to-end, source data intact, retention still enforced at 7 archives) after each restart.
actions_performed: Created /srv/inventory/data on node2 with sample inventory CSV files (source data did not pre-exist)
Set up passwordless SSH from node1 (antrieb) to node2 using cluster-provided keypair
Created /var/backups/inventory on node1, owned by antrieb
Wrote /usr/local/bin/backup-inventory.sh on node1: pulls tar stream from node2 over SSH into a dated archive, logs via logger, prunes to the 7 most recent archives
Installed /etc/cron.d/backup-inventory to run the script nightly at 02:00 as user antrieb
Manually ran the script to verify a successful backup and validated archive contents matched source data
Simulated 8 days of dated archives to test and confirm 7-day retention pruning (oldest removed, logged via journalctl)
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, cron status, backup archives, source data hashes) on both nodes
Rebooted node1 via shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified cron/SSH/backup script/retention all functioned correctly post-restart

Rebooted node2 via shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified source data intact, then ran the full backup end-to-end from node1 confirming SSH, script, cron config, and retention still work after both restarts
